_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::heat#5 — BDF2 needs no hand-written start-up, and 4C gives you no way to see the one it already does. The same 3-D HEX8 heat deck under TIMEINTEGR 'BDF2' and under 'One_Step_Theta' with THETA 1.0 (which IS backward Euler): after ONE step the two agree to the last printed digit (1.75354251012145718e-01 both), after two (3.03303489655998737e-01 vs 2.89998581151961199e-01) and after three (3.90141172605912911e-01 vs 3.70066213493452145e-01) they differ. The later-step disagreement is what stops the first observation being vacuous — if BDF2 never engaged, every step would agree. And the step header of the BDF2 run says 'BDF2       STEP = 1/3' on the very step that is not BDF2, with the same word on all three steps (BDF2_BANNER_STEPS=3) and no start-up announcement anywhere (STARTUP_ANNOUNCED=0). Matches src/scatra/4C_scatra_timint_bdf2.cpp, where set_old_part_of_righthandside uses theta=1.0 for step 1 and 2/3 thereafter. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: run the 'BDF2' arm as One_Step_Theta too. Every step then agrees, LATER_STEPS_DIFFER flips to no and the printed BDF2 banner disappears, so the fixture must go red — that assertion is what proves BDF2 really engages after step 1.
break the comparison the other way: make the control something that is NOT backward Euler. The one-step equality fails and the fixture must go red.
